headline_marked: Sri Lanka [[chase down 430 to beat England]] in Rawalpindi record-breaker
headline: Sri Lanka chase down 430 to beat England in Rawalpindi record-breaker
summary: Sri Lanka achieved the second-highest successful chase in ODI history, while England's Harry Brook smashed the fastest double century ever recorded.
details: Sri Lanka beat England by two wickets in Rawalpindi, successfully chasing a mammoth target of 430 runs. This marks the second-highest successful chase in men's ODI history, surpassed only by South Africa's 435-run chase in 2006.

England's Harry Brook delivered a historic performance, smashing an unbeaten 202 off just 114 balls. This is the fastest double century in men's ODI cricket, breaking the previous record held by Shubman Gill.

Brook's innings was a series of firsts: he became the first England batter to score an ODI double century and the first to do so in Pakistan. He also became the first batter to score a double century in a losing cause.
England posted a total of 429 for four, which is the highest ODI total ever recorded in Pakistan. England has now reached 400+ runs eight times in ODIs, level with South Africa.

The match saw an aggregate of 859 runs, the second-highest in an ODI match. Eight different batters scored fifty or more, equalling the record for the most individual fifty-plus scores in a single game.
Joe Root also reached a major milestone, becoming the first England batter to reach 8,000 runs in men's ODIs, becoming the 34th batter overall to reach the milestone.

headline_marked: 3,000 tourists [[rescued from Sajek]] after gunfire and road blockade
headline: 3,000 tourists rescued from Sajek after gunfire and road blockade
summary: Army and police escorted stranded travelers to safety after clashes between security forces and protesters demanding the removal of an armed group.
details: Around 3,000 tourists were escorted to Khagrachhari yesterday after being stranded by a road blockade near Sajek Valley in Rangamati. The evacuation was conducted jointly by the army and police following reports of gunfire and clashes.
The blockade was enforced by the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association to demand the removal of an armed group affiliated with the PCJSS.

According to the ISPR, protesters allegedly instigated by UPDF members threw bricks and stones at law enforcers and tourists. The ISPR claimed armed UPDF members fired 30-40 shots, prompting the army to return fire in self-defence to protect the tourists.
Conversely, UPDF spokesperson Angya Marma denied the gunfight, alleging that security forces fired shots to break a peaceful blockade and used truncheon charges against civilians.
The convener of the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee alleged that over 57 civilians were injured by security forces and that law enforcers prevented the injured from reaching hospitals.
Law enforcement officials confirmed that five army personnel and two police members were injured during the clashes. No tourists were reported injured, according to Rangamati SP Muhammad Abdur Rakib.
The district administration had suspended tourist travel to the valley on Wednesday evening and ordered all tourists to leave by 4:00pm yesterday to avoid further escalation.
caption:
3,000 tourists were stranded in the hills of Sajek after a road blockade turned into a gunfight.

Around 3,000 tourists were escorted to Khagrachhari yesterday after being stranded by a road blockade near Sajek Valley in Rangamati. The evacuation was conducted jointly by the army and police following reports of gunfire and clashes.

The blockade was enforced by the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association to demand the removal of an armed group affiliated with the PCJSS.

According to the ISPR, protesters allegedly instigated by UPDF members threw bricks and stones at law enforcers and tourists. The ISPR claimed armed UPDF members fired 30-40 shots, prompting the army to return fire in self-defence to protect the tourists.

Conversely, UPDF spokesperson Angya Marma denied the gunfight, alleging that security forces fired shots to break a peaceful blockade and used truncheon charges against civilians.

The convener of the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee alleged that over 57 civilians were injured by security forces and that law enforcers prevented the injured from reaching hospitals.

Law enforcement officials confirmed that five army personnel and two police members were injured during the clashes. No tourists were reported injured, according to Rangamati SP Muhammad Abdur Rakib.

The district administration had suspended tourist travel to the valley on Wednesday evening and ordered all tourists to leave by 4:00pm yesterday to avoid further escalation.
